context: Tatsuya-country recommends an old-school folk song to Sho-young.
purpose: Elder sharing musical tradition with child.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: Sho — I'll teach you an old song from back when.
lines.style: Slow, patient opening. Deep Tohoku drawl. Warm fondness in the voice — the sound of a memory he's carried for decades. Unhurried, like there's all the time in the world.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: うん、おじいちゃん、どんな歌?
lines.style: Bright curiosity, but held soft. Child's voice eager to listen. Leans in slightly. Genuine wonder, not performance.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 田んぼで草、生えてる頃、歌っとった。
lines.en: When the weeds were growing tall in the paddy fields — that's when I used to sing it.
lines.style: Gentle, drifting tone. Eyes distant. Each phrase lands like a memory settling. Slow, deliberate pacing. The voice of someone standing in a field he can still see.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 農薬、ない頃、自然がいっぱい?
lines.en: Back when there were no chemicals — when nature was everywhere?
lines.style: Soft, thinking tone. Not quite a question — more like Sho is piecing something together out loud. Perceptive beyond his years. Warm respect underneath the curiosity.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: Yeah — we sang it with our whole hearts back then.
lines.style: Affirming nod in the voice. Tenderness settling deeper. The word 「心」 carries the weight — 'heart' not as sentiment but as sincerity. Quiet conviction.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 懐かしい時代やな、おじいちゃんの。
lines.en: Your time was different, wasn't it, grandpa.
lines.style: Soft wonder and respect braided together. Not mourning — reverence. The child recognizing something precious in what he's hearing. Small voice, big understanding.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: Come on — let's sing it together.
lines.style: Warm invitation. A gentle opening, like extending a hand. The Tohoku lilt softens the offer. Unhurried. An invitation with no pressure — just an old man wanting to share.
